equity_bridge.item: H1 FY2027 owner FCF already banked in the 30-Sep-2026 net debt
equity_bridge.note: FY0 is FY2026, so year 1 is the whole of FY2027, but the 30 September 2026 net debt already reflects H1 FY2027's cash generation (OCF 2.834 - capex 0.050 + disposals 0.001 - lease principal 0.760 = 2.025; ties to the 7.05 debt repayment = 5.000 raise + 2.025 + 0.025 cash drawdown). Deducted so that half-year is not counted twice. Equivalent to using 31 March 2026 net debt pro forma for the raise (23.476).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue (FY2023 227.4 to FY2026 165.1) and equity (34.6 to 17.9, including the FY2024 11.0 goodwill impairment) CAGRs are both deeply negative; EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined because the end values are negative (FY2026 EPS -$0.062 in dollars; owner FCF -0.78). Historical CAGRs describe the FY2023-26 downturn and are not used as a growth driver. Equity rose to 22.7 at 30-Sep-2026 only because of the 5.0 raise.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF less SBC less lease principal (lease interest is already inside operating cash flow): FY2021 17.9, FY2022 7.4, FY2023 1.3, FY2024 -0.9, FY2025 -3.9, FY2026 -0.8. H1 FY2027: 2.0, of which 1.3 was a seasonal working-capital release. SBC is under 0.25 in every year, so reported and SBC-adjusted growth do not diverge; the collapse is cyclical.

scenario_narratives.base: The NZ labour market recovers gradually through 2027 as economists expect. FY2027 lands on guidance (pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA ~3.3), helped by a first half already reported. FY2028 comes in around 5.0 rather than management's 6.9: White Collar permanent and contracting volumes recover, but Wellington public-sector work stays thin, entry-level and clerical placements at Madison and Absolute IT keep leaking to AI tools, and a new CEO takes over mid-recovery. Margins settle at the pre-downturn average (4.5% post-IFRS-16, ~3.2% pre) by FY2030 and revenue regains the FY2023 peak in nominal terms around FY2034. Owner FCF matures near 2% of revenue, roughly 4-5 a year against 21.5 of bank debt: enough to service and slowly repay it, with a modest residual for equity.
scenario_narratives.bull: Management's plan is delivered: 6.9 of pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA in FY2028 as Blue Collar rides infrastructure and civil-works demand for higher-skilled labour, White Collar permanent placement revenue (up 28% in H1 FY2027, the highest-margin line) keeps compounding, and the 'economic benefit to New Zealand' procurement test wins public-sector panels from Randstad and Hays. CRM automation and candidate-facing AI lift consultant productivity so margins pass the FY2022 level and reach 5.8% post-IFRS-16. Debt falls quickly, the facility is refinanced on normal terms before April 2028 and dividends resume.
scenario_narratives.bear: The recovery stalls after one good half. An energy-cost or geopolitical shock (the risk management itself flagged) or post-election fiscal restraint holds unemployment near 5.5%; H2 FY2027 is flat and FY2028 slips. Pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA sits near 3, about what bank interest costs, so nothing is left to repay debt. The cumulative-EBITDA and leverage covenants set with ASB for the facility to April 2028 come under pressure during a CEO transition overseen by a three-person board, and the outcome is another discounted raise underwritten by the Hull Family Trust (already ~65%) or a take-out at a low price. The model's negative equity value in this scenario is that outcome: the business is worth less than its bank debt.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Accordant is a 100%-NZ staffing group with no moat, low-single-digit margins and ~21.5 of bank debt against a market value well below that. The equity is a geared claim on a labour-market recovery: enterprise value in the base case is ~35 and debt takes about two-thirds of it, so a 10% change in enterprise value moves the equity by roughly 30%. The DCF is built mid-cycle - not from the FY2024-26 trough and not from management's FY2028 target - with the full lease cash cost charged and a plain 12% NZD discount rate. Risk is carried by the scenarios (a bear path in which the equity is worth nothing) and by a 35% bear weight, not by the discount rate.
valuation_philosophy.limited_liability_memo: The bear case produces a negative equity value and the engine carries it into the weighted value as negative. Flooring the bear case at zero instead gives a weighted value of 0.45 x base + 0.20 x bull, shown in the reconciliation block as 'floored_weighted_memo'. The floored figure is the more defensible estimate of what a share is worth; the unfloored figure is the one comparable with the prior version and with the rest of the folder.
valuation_philosophy.what_changed_vs_prior: See reconciliation. Three things moved the value: (1) the WACC stack was removed (17/15.5/19% to a single 12%), by far the largest item; (2) the year-1 and year-2 drivers were re-anchored to H1 FY2027 actuals and guidance and the working-capital drag was cut to match the balance sheet; (3) the lease charge was corrected upward to include lease interest and the right-of-use tax shield was removed, which lowers value. Mature margins, years 2-10 growth, capex, tax, terminal growth and scenario weights are unchanged.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gearing: equity is the thin residual after ~21.5 of bank debt, so small errors in the mature margin swing the per-share value by multiples. A mature post-IFRS-16 margin of 4.0% instead of 4.5% in the base case removes most of the equity value.
The discount-rate change is a methodology judgment. At the prior version's 17% the base case equity is worth approximately nothing; see the sensitivity grid and required-return table.
FY2028 guidance (6.9 pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA) is haircut to ~5.0 in the base case; management has moved its recovery timing twice before.
Covenants (cumulative EBITDA, leverage, interest cover) and the April 2028 facility maturity: a breach turns the bear case into a dilutive raise at a price set by the controlling holder.

Hull Family Trust at ~64.9% with a three-person board: minorities have little say over the terms of any further raise or take-out, and the free float is tiny, so the quoted price is set by very small volumes.
Goodwill 31.6 and other intangibles 12.7 against equity of 22.7: tangible book is negative, so there is no asset floor under the DCF.
Per-share outputs are rounded to whole cents by the build, a material rounding step at this share price.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 0.13-0.33. Last trade is two sessions old and daily volume is in the hundreds to low thousands of shares.
data_sources.financials: AGL.NZ_Metrics.csv (rebuilt 2026-11-19); H1 FY2027 interim report (six months to 30 September 2026, unaudited, authorised 28 October 2026) for balance sheet, cash flow and lease payments; FY2026 Annual Report for the D&A split, tax note and share-based payments; March 2026 capital-raise presentation for the FY2027/FY2028 EBITDA estimates.

prior_version.note: Legacy hand-built DCF (no Drivers file). Price was refreshed to 0.146 on 2026-08-12 without a rebuild. Share count was already post-raise (67.659m); net debt was a pro-forma 24.0.

bridge.item: Prior weighted IV (2026-07-31, legacy hand-built model)
Anchor refresh: effective net debt 24.000 pro forma -> 23.476 (21.451 at 30-Sep-2026 plus the 2.025 of H1 FY2027 owner FCF deducted in the equity bridge); share count unchanged at 67.659m
bridge.note: The prior version assumed ~0.5 of raise costs; the interim shows 5.000 received and 5.000 added to share capital.

bridge.item: Engine migration: the prior model's recorded drivers re-run through build-dcf
bridge.note: Not a judgment change. The prior file's projections used a D&A line below its own recorded da_pct path (2.22% of revenue in year 1 against a recorded 2.30%; 1.8% in FY2033 against a recorded 2.8%), so its stated drivers reproduce a slightly higher value than it reported.

bridge.item: Methodology: lease charge corrected to principal + interest (1.1-1.2% -> 1.3-1.4% of revenue) and tax shield limited to D&A ex right-of-use depreciation

Driver changes on new evidence: year-1 growth to 7/9/4% (H1 FY2027 +8%), EBITDA margin ramp re-anchored to H1 actuals and FY2027-28 guidance (mature levels unchanged), working-capital drag 12% -> 5% of incremental revenue
Methodology: single 12% NZD WACC in place of the 17.0 / 15.5 / 19.0% stacked-premium, per-scenario rates (risk charged once, in the scenarios and weights)
Price move 0.166 -> current (no effect on intrinsic value)

bridge.note: Ties to probability_weighted.weighted_iv, which the build rounds to whole cents. floored_weighted_memo (bear equity floored at zero, limited liability): 0.1669.

reconciliation.bridge_method: Each step is a separate make build-dcf run with the changes applied cumulatively in the order listed; per-share values are taken from the build's equity values (0.1m precision) rather than its whole-cent per-share outputs. The engine-migration line is the residual between the prior hand-built model and the same drivers run through the engine, after the net-debt change (which is exact: 0.524 / 67.659).

unchanged_assumptions.would_move_on: FY2027 full-year revenue and the first FY2028 trading update; a second half below +3% would pull base years 2-3 down.

unchanged_assumptions.assumption: Mature EBITDA margin (base 4.5%, bull 5.8%, bear 3.2%, post-IFRS-16)
unchanged_assumptions.status: level unchanged; base now reached in FY2030 not FY2034
unchanged_assumptions.would_move_on: Two consecutive halves of pre-IFRS-16 margin above 3.5% (raise base) or FY2028 EBITDA below 4 (lower it).
A disclosed technology capex programme; actual spend is running at a third of this.
A new executive incentive scheme for the incoming CEO.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash-flow reconciliation: equity-settled share-based payments $78k (H1 FY2027: $31k). No net-share-settlement tax line. Under 0.1% of revenue in every year.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-17T23:31:03Z last trade (NZX regular session; no trade printed 18-19 Nov, thinly traded)
inputs.share_count_basis: 67.659m = 34,325,542 pre-raise ordinary shares + 33,333,334 issued in the May 2026 rights offer. Includes 406,809 treasury shares and 800,000 restricted scheme shares, so it is the fully diluted count. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and no further non-SBC issuance is modelled in base or bull (the bear case's negative equity value is what a further rescue raise would look like).
inputs.wacc_rationale: 12.0% in every scenario, built in NZD: NZ 10-year government yield ~4.5% + ~6% equity risk premium x levered beta ~1.5-1.6 gives a cost of equity ~14%; pre-tax bank debt cost ~9% (H1 FY2027 bank interest 1.203 on ~25m average borrowings annualises to ~9.6%; FY2026 2.432 on ~29.8m is 8.2%), ~6.5% after 28% tax; at a 65/35 target equity/debt mix that is ~11.5%, rounded up to 12%, the top of the 11-12% NZ small-cap base the prior version itself started from. METHODOLOGY CHANGE vs the prior build, which used 17.0% base / 15.5% bull / 19.0% bear by stacking four premiums (illiquidity, cyclicality, leverage, governance) on that base and then varying WACC by scenario. Those same risks are already carried in the flows (a bear path that never recovers, margins capped at mid-cycle) and in the 35% bear weight, so the stack charged them two or three times (owner-fcf-adaptations (f)). Risk now lives in the scenarios and weights; the discount rate is a plain NZD small-cap rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as an operating cost: the full lease cash payment (principal + interest, both off the cash-flow statement) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, lease liabilities (12.073 at 30-Sep-2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt, and D&A is ex right-of-use depreciation. FY2026 lease cash was 2.131 principal + 0.542 interest = 2.673 (1.62% of revenue); H1 FY2027 was 0.760 + 0.385 = 1.145 (1.29%). The ebitda_margin_path is therefore POST-IFRS-16 EBITDA (comparable to the Metrics CSV EBITDA column); management's guidance is PRE-IFRS-16, and pre = post less the lease charge. CORRECTION vs the prior build, which deducted lease principal only (1.1% of revenue), omitted lease interest, and took a tax shield on total D&A including right-of-use depreciation.
inputs.net_debt_note: Net bank debt at 30 September 2026: borrowings 21.600 less cash 0.149 = 21.451 (H1 FY2027 interim balance sheet), after the 5.000 rights-offer proceeds and 7.050 of repayments. The equity_bridge deducts the 2.025 of H1 FY2027 owner FCF already inside that figure, because year 1 of the projection is the whole of FY2027. Effective net debt for the valuation is 23.476, identical to 31 March 2026 net debt (28.650 - 0.174) pro forma for the raise. September is also the seasonal working-capital low (receivables 16.2 vs 20.0 at March).
inputs.guidance_anchor: Capital-raise presentation (March 2026): Group EBITDA pre-IFRS-16 of ~3.2 for FY2027 and ~6.9 for FY2028 (FY2026 estimate 1.3; actuals FY2022 8.8, FY2023 6.6, FY2024 3.5, FY2025 -1.0). H1 FY2027 pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA was 1.8, 'modestly ahead of target'; post-IFRS-16 EBITDA was 2.954 (loss before tax -0.302 + finance costs 1.594 + D&A 1.662), a 3.34% margin on revenue of 88.545 (+8% YoY).
inputs.eps_dps_scale_note: EPS and DPS in the Metrics CSV are in dollars (rescaled from cents on 2026-11-19). Neither is an input to this model.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, three scenarios, probability-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical', with the adaptations for leases, WACC currency, working-capital sign and charging risk once). Accordant is a staffing/recruitment operating company whose value is a thin stream of free cash flow against bank debt; it is not a bank, REIT or holdco in the valuation sense. Same model family as the prior (hand-built, legacy) valuation of 2026-07-31; this version moves it onto the Drivers/build-dcf route. FY0 is FY2026 (year to 31 March 2026); year 1 is FY2027, the guidance year, half of which is already reported. Horizon 10 years; owner-FCF margin is flat from about year 5-6. SBC is ~0.05% of revenue, so house and street are effectively the same number and band_position carries no information for this ticker. No buybacks, no dividends since FY2023; the flat share count is a convention that costs almost nothing here because SBC is immaterial. PRECISION: the build rounds per-share values to whole cents, which is coarse for a stock priced in the low teens of cents; the reconciliation bridge is computed from the unrounded-to-0.1m equity values. LIMITED LIABILITY: the bear case equity value is negative and is carried into the weighted value as a negative number, as in the prior version. A holder cannot lose more than the price paid, so the weighted value floored at zero for the bear case is reported in valuation_philosophy as a memo.

bear.growth_rates_note: Year 1 4.0%: H1's +8% is banked, H2 is flat on last year. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED from the prior version (0.5-1.0%): the recovery stalls and revenue stays ~175-185 for a decade.
bear.ebitda_margin_path_note: Post-IFRS-16. FY2027 3.0% (pre-IFRS-16 ~2.8, guidance missed in H2), FY2028 2.8% on a setback year, then a slow climb to the prior version's UNCHANGED mature 3.2% - a pre-IFRS-16 margin of only ~1.8%, roughly the FY2024 level, forever.
bear.other_note: Lease charge 1.4% flat (fixed cost on a non-growing base). Capex 0.30% and terminal growth 1.5% UNCHANGED. Working-capital capture -4% (prior -10%).

base.growth_rates_note: Year 1 (FY2027) 7.0%: H1 was +8% and H2 is assumed +6% on H2 FY2026's 83.1. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED from the prior version (4.5, 5.0, 4.5, 4.0, 3.5, 3.0, 2.8, 2.5, 2.5). FY2036 revenue ~243, against the FY2023 peak of 227.4 and FY2018's 279.3, in nominal dollars.
base.ebitda_margin_path_note: Post-IFRS-16. FY2027 3.2% = guidance-year pre-IFRS-16 EBITDA of ~3.3 (guidance 3.2, H1 1.8) plus the 1.3% lease charge. FY2028 4.0% = pre-IFRS-16 ~5.0, a deliberate haircut to management's 6.9, which would need a 3.7% pre-IFRS-16 margin (FY2022's peak-cycle level was 4.0%, FY2023's 2.9%) and comes from a team that has pushed its recovery timing back twice. Mature 4.5% is UNCHANGED from the prior version (FY2018/20/22/23 average 4.45%) but is reached in FY2030 rather than FY2034, because H1 FY2027 already printed 3.34% against the prior path's 2.73% for the year.
base.da_pct_path_note: Ex right-of-use depreciation. FY2026 PPE depreciation 0.481 + intangible amortisation 0.886 = 1.367 (0.83% of revenue); H1 FY2027 runs ~0.6%. Glides to 0.35%, equal to capex, as acquired intangibles amortise off.
base.capex_pct_path_note: 0.35% UNCHANGED from the prior version. Actual PPE spend has been 0.1% of revenue (FY2026 0.183, H1 FY2027 0.050); the excess is an allowance for the technology/AI spend management describes.
base.wc_capture_pct_note: -5% of incremental revenue (growth consumes cash: receivables exceed payables). CHANGED from the prior -12%: net working capital on the balance sheet is only 0.4-1.3% of revenue (30-Sep-2026 receivables 16.197 less payables 15.304 and contract liabilities 0.260; 31-Mar-2026 19.968 less 17.254 and 0.545), because wages, PAYE, GST and holiday-pay accruals fund most of the receivable book. 5% is still several times the balance-sheet ratio.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_note: NZ statutory 28% flat, UNCHANGED. No material unrecognised tax losses found (FY2025-26 losses were largely carried back or refunded; the balance sheet shows a net deferred tax liability of 0.579), so no shelter is modelled. Tax is never credited on a loss.
base.terminal_note: Terminal growth 1.8% UNCHANGED. Cap 12x FCF (cyclical setting); Gordon binds at ~10x.

bull.growth_rates_note: Year 1 9.0% (H2 accelerates to ~+10%); years 2-10 UNCHANGED from the prior version. FY2036 revenue ~266, still below FY2018.
bull.ebitda_margin_path_note: Post-IFRS-16. FY2027 3.4% and FY2028 4.9% are management's guidance delivered in full (pre-IFRS-16 ~3.7 and ~6.9). Mature 5.8% is UNCHANGED from the prior version and is reached in FY2033 as before; it implies a pre-IFRS-16 margin of ~4.7%, above anything since IFRS 16 was adopted, so it needs the AI/automation productivity story to work as well as the cycle.
bull.other_note: Lease charge falls from 1.3% to 1.1% of revenue on operating leverage over a largely fixed property footprint. Capex 0.40% and terminal growth 2.0% UNCHANGED. Working-capital capture -6% (prior -14%), same evidence as base.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 35% bear / 45% base / 20% bull, UNCHANGED from the prior version and deliberately not the 15/50/35 house default. Bear 35%: three straight loss-making years, a rescue raise six months ago that fell short of its 6.7 target, tangible book value still negative, covenants live until April 2028, a controlling holder and a retiring CEO with no successor named. Base 45%: H1 FY2027 delivered against guidance and bank debt is down 7.0 since March, which is real evidence, but it is one half-year. Bull 20%: it needs the cycle, the full FY2028 guidance and an unproven AI margin uplift together. H1's delivery argues for a lower bear weight and the governance changes since July argue for a higher one; I have left them to offset. Evidence that would move it: FY2027 guidance met at the May 2027 result with a successor CEO in place would take bear to ~25%; an H2 miss or a covenant waiver would take it to 45%+.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
